text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000162 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, but the few returned charts support the billed level, so the records are too thin to call this upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 rate is not confined to sicker patients. It runs at roughly two to three times the all-provider share in every complexity tier, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. That points to a provider-wide billing habit rather than a panel-driven effect. The records review cuts the other way: the handful of documented 99215s all support the billed level, and only one note claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a lab or test line. However, with so few documented 99215 claims, the sample is too small to be reassuring. Two of the supported examples are low-complexity visits documented as high MDM: C0082488 (no chronic conditions, abdominal pain, minutes not recorded) and C0082768. Patient M0034839, who has only hyperlipidemia, appears on three sampled 99215s (C0082702, C0082768, C0082771). Charts that consistently read high MDM for simple presentations could reflect genuinely complex acute visits or templated documentation. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with M0034839's visits and the 0-condition visits (C0082395, C0082465, C0082728, C0082909). They should then check whether the high-MDM notes are individualized and whether time is recorded."}
